newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Caldera takes a walk to show he is fine.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Caldera takes a walk to show he is fine.

text.p: Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera, dogged by persistent rumours that his health is failing, went for a short walk in the capital on Thursday to prove he is alive and well.

Accompanied by his wife and members of his Cabinet, the 81-year-old president slowly paced the 500-yard (metres) distance between Congress and Miraflores presidential palace in the historic centre of Caracas.
"That is President Caldera himself. It's not a clone, nor has he been revived because he never died," the usually impassive Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff joked with reporters.
Local and international markets were awash with rumours on Wednesday that Caldera, Latin America's oldest leader had died.
Before taking the walk, Caldera made a 45-minute address to legislators in which he reaffirmed his commitment to continuing an economic reform programme launched a year ago.

He read his prepared text in a breathless, slurred voice but said he planned to complete his term in December 1998, "even though the astrologer won't like it" in reference to a local astrologer who predicted recently that Caldera would not see the end of 1997.
